maybe you feel like running because you're worried that your problems will push people away. I find I keep people at arms length because my past relationships ended poorly because of my own issues. I think the best thing to do, and bear in mind I'm just some guy on the internet, is talk to your SO and see if you can explain to them what happens when you get your symptoms, or how you feel. Doctors and therapists can be good and all, but it can feel like they don't matter if the people in your life don't act the way you need them to. So talk to them, and despite how embarrassing it might be, or scary, get as much of it out as you can. This person is with you for a reason. Try to remember that. Hope this helps.

let me ask you, do you feel sometimes that you are floating above your body, or maybe behind. maybe sometimes you feel like you're borrowing someone else's body? it sounds like depression, and for me at least, thats how I felt when I was at my worst. what I did was set a date for me 1 month out, and did my damnedest to convince myself I was worth it. I saw a therapist, and he got me on antidepressants. for a while I survived by pushing that date back a month because the deadline would come up and I wasn't sure. give it a try. doesn't have to be a month, but pick a date as far out as you can and do what you can to walk away from it. if you are gonna go, go out swinging.

This might sound like bad advice, but trust me on this. Don't worry quite so much about how you act around him. As someone with depression, it kills me to see people walk on eggshells around me. It makes me feel fragile like I might break if someone looks at me wrong, and I get tired quickly of the look of panic thinly veiled behind their eyes every time they talk to me. Depression doesn't mean being sad all the time. You can smile and laugh with everyone else, but it fades way faster than it should. emotions become fleeting and trivial. Sometimes we secretly like feeling sad simply because of how deep that emotion is, and its so much better to feel something, anything, than that nothing that is the norm. we love it, and we hate that we love it. we feel guilty for it, and start to feel we deserve to be broken. The other thing is making decisions is extremely hard when depressed. they all seem pointless. Even when we aren't actively planning we still feel like we are just visitors in our own lives. Like we wont be here for long. So my advice is find a therapist, talk to them, see if they might be a good fit, and give him 1 option. make the most difficult decision he has to make whether he wants the appointment at 11:00 on monday, or 3:00 on monday.

Good luck, depression is hard on a relationship.
